articles.body:
Pamela Hurts, the mother of Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts, is a longtime educator.

On Monday, she revealed that some of her students wrote cards of support for her and her son after the news that Hurts has been diagnosed with blood clots and will miss the remainder of the 2026 season:

"Just a reminder, y'all. Be grateful," she said in a previous social media post following her son's diagnosis. "Be grateful for where you are and what you have because your life could change at a blink of an eye. Be grateful. What are you grateful for?"

articles.title: B/R Experts Week 8 NFL Power Rankings
articles.summary: Seven weeks into the 2026 season, the NFL landscape is taking shape. Just don't ask which shape it is—because this triacontadigon is constantly changing.
articles.body:
Seven weeks into the 2026 season, the NFL landscape is taking shape. Just don't ask which shape it is—because this triacontadigon is constantly changing.

Heading into Week 7, three teams held perfect records. Now, just one team has an unblemished record—and if you had the Minnesota Vikings as the league's last unbeaten squad, then go buy Powerball tickets, because apparently you can predict the future.

At the opposite end of the spectrum, after the Miami Dolphins downed the New York Jets there's just one team still searching for win No. 1—and it's a Los Angeles Chargers squad labeled by many a playoff contender entering the season. In between, there are surprises galore—for better and for worse.

Another wild week of NFL action has shaken the league's pecking order—especially at the top. And just as they do every week, Bleacher Report NFL analysts Gary Davenport , Kris Knox , Maurice Moton and Brent Sobleski have gathered to try to make sense of it all by ranking all 32 teams from worst to first.

There's a new No. 1—and they didn't even play in Week 7.

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN | CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND | JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN | NE | NYG | NO | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SEA | SF | TB | TEN | WAS

The Los Angeles Chargers lost during their bye week, because the team sat at home and watched as they became the league's only winless team.

The marriage between quarterback Justin Herbert and offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel simply hasn't worked despite preseason excitement over the pairing. As a result, the Chargers will likely look different coming out of their bye.

"Definitely looking at volume and where you can make [the offensive playbook] to where the players can understand," head coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters . At 0-6, something has to be done in an attempt to improve the situation. However, the Chargers' start has been so poor the organization should already be looking toward its future. -- Sobleski

There are no moral victories in the NFL. The Tennessee Titans are no doubt kicking themselves after Sunday's last-second loss to Cleveland—especially given that the team was up 14-0 and one yard from going up 21-7.

But not that long the Titans weren't even that competitive. There are bright spots for the team. Running back Tony Pollard had his best game of the season, rushing for 129 yards and three touchdowns. Rookie receiver Carnell Tate remained a focal point in the passing game, catching five passes for 69 yards.

On the flip side though, cam Ward continues to be inconsistent (at best) throwing the football, and both Ward and Tate turned the ball over.

The Titans appear headed toward a top-five pick in next year's draft—and a decision.

Is Ward "The Guy?" Or do the Titans need to draft a quarterback two years after taking him No. 1 overall? – Davenport

Week 7 Result: Won at New York Jets 28-25

The Miami Dolphins looked like an entirely different football team coming out of their Week 6 bye, at least offensively. Miami got another big game from running back Ollie Gordon II and got a strong dual-threat performance from quarterback Malik Willis (208 passing yards, 37 rushing yards, 3 total TDs).

Miami's defense still surrenders too many easy yards, and a win over the rival New York Jets won't rocket them toward the playoff picture. However, Sunday's win was huge for a couple of reasons.

This season is about evaluating Willis as a potential long-term quarterback and developing young skill players like Gordon, Caleb Douglas, and Chris Bell. It's also about developing an identity under new head coach Jeff Hafley.

The Dolphins have played like a scrappy underdog all season, and it finally paid off with a big divisional win. It probably won't be the only upset that the Dolphins deliver in 2026. -- Knox

There have been rampant rumors that the Colts could sell veteran players if the losses continue piling up, with players like running back Jonathan Taylor, defensive tackle DeForest Buckner and guard Quentin Nelson all mentioned as veterans who could be dealt.

After a dispiriting loss to the Vikings that dropped the Colts to 2-5, the team is that much closer to just blowing things up—a stunning fall from grace for a team that started the 2025 campaign 8-2.

It has become clear that hot start was a mirage. The "win now" trade for cornerback Sauce Gardner last year and the extension handed to quarterback Daniel Jones were massive mistakes—mistakes that cost Chris Ballard his job.

Now, the path forward appears to be starting over in 2027—and using veterans to stockpile draft capital. – Davenport

We're getting to time to figure out if Carson Beck is a thing or not.

He probably isn't. But it's just about time to find out.

We know what the Cardinals are with Jacoby Brissett under center—bad. There are some weapons in the desert in wideout Michaeel Wilson, tight end Trey McBride and running back Jeremiyah Love. But the defense is inconsistent at best, and the only games the team has won are at SoFi Stadium.

The Cardinals do not play home games there.

Beck probably isn't the long-term answer at quarterback, but he was a three-year starter at Georgia and then Miami. The Redbirds thought enough of him to spend a Day 2 pick on him.

And if they're going to get him some game reps, now is the time—after the Cowboys' non-existent defense in Week 8, the Cardinals face Seattle, the Rams and Kansas City.

This will be a 3-8 team (at best) by the end of November. -- Davenport

The Washington Commanders couldn't get out of their own way with poor situational awareness over the last two weeks. They should've had a chance to kick a game-winning field goal in Week 5, and head coach Dan Quinn had to answer questions about a fourth-down sequence in Week 6.

To make matters worse, wideout Terry McLaurin will miss the remainder of the season with a torn patellar tendon.

The Commanders' season is on the brink of disaster. This team needed a Week 7 bye to regroup, as Quinn may be coaching to save his job. Though in a mediocre division, Washington can still make a run for the NFC East title. -- Moton

Changes may be coming for the New York Jets, and it's fair to wonder how significant they could be.

We have seen some positives in New York this season. The Jets have two wins after notching just three in all of last season. They've also seen early returns from young players like David Bailey, Omar Cooper Jr., Mason Taylor, and Kenyon Sadiq. Their defense has been good enough to at least keep them in games.

However, the offensive chemistry has been spotty at best, and head coach Aaron Glenn continues to struggle with situational management. New York is now 0-8 in AFC East games since Glenn took over last season, which is unacceptable for a franchise that hasn't won a division title since 2002.

The Jets own three 2027 first-round picks and are widely expected to draft their next QB of the future in the offseason. It's getting harder to believe that they won't be in the market for a new coaching staff, too. -- Knox

Week 7 Result: Lost vs. Pittsburgh 16-10

Heading into 2026, the New Orleans Saints felt like a team that was poised to make a big jump. After seven weeks, it's clear that New Orleans is still at least a year away from being a legitimate contender.

Tyler Shough showed franchise-quarterback potential late in his rookie campaign, and he's largely built on last year's success this season. However, he hasn't been perfect enough to consistently carry an offense that has struggled to move the ball on the ground. On Sunday, he made a couple of big red-zone mistakes that cost the Saints in a very tight contest.

Defensively, New Orleans has been a total disappointment. The Saints entered Week 7 ranked 29th in yards allowed and 31st in points allowed. While they did hold the Pittsburgh Steelers to 16 points, they coughed up 343 total yards and allowed Pittsburgh to convert 10 of 16 third-down attempts.

Franchise owner Gayle Benson told reporters earlier in the season that the Saints "must do better."

If things don't start to change on the field before the end of the season, changes to the front office could come after it. -- Knox

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers have only won two games this season, but they're 1-0 in the NFC South and made a bit of a statement in Week 7.

Tampa's defense has been good enough to keep the Bucs in games for most of the season. Their ground game has looked elite in each of their two victories, and quarterback Baker Mayfield returned from his dislocated thumb during Sunday's romp over the Carolina Panthers.

The Panthers previously looked like a team that might run away with the NFC South. Now, things appear wide open, and the Bucs very much feel like a team that could slide back into the mix and steal the division.

Next week's matchup with the 3-4 Atlanta Falcons will be huge. -- Knox

The Philadelphia Eagles will welcome back Saquon Barkley after a two-game absence with a hamstring injury. However, the Eagles will be without lead wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks Monday night.

Backup quarterback Tanner McKee, making his fourth career start and his second of the season in place of Jalen Hurts (blood clots), may hand off more than he throws downfield in an NFC East showdown with the Dallas Cowboys. -- Moton

Week 7 Result: Lost vs. New York Giants 27-21 (OT)

After peeling off back-to-back wins, the Houston Texans appeared to have something cooking after four straight losses to open the season.

There are a number of reasons why the Texans have struggled. But the most surprising has to be the team's defensive collapse. Last year, Houston led the league in total defense and ranked first in the AFC in scoring defense. This season, Houston's defense has been average—on a good day. The Texans allowed 420 yards of offense in Sunday's overtime loss, including 188 yards and four scores on the ground.

The offense isn't without blame—taking on a Giants team short its best edge-rusher and green dot linebacker, the Texans had just 237 yards of offense and were 3-for-12 on third down.

Houston heads into their bye week facing an unpleasant reality—there will be no return to the playoffs in 2026. – Davenport

What's happened to the Dallas Cowboys offense? The Cowboys' Dak Prescott-led unit, with wide receivers CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and running back Javonte Williams, has averaged 14.5 points over the last two weeks. Dallas has more turnovers—five—than touchdowns—four in that span .

It won't be easy against Philadelphia Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, but the Cowboys must rediscover their offensive mojo to close the gap on the New York Giants in the NFC East. -- Moton

Week 5 Result: Lost vs. Los Angeles Rams 35-21

The feelgood start to the Las Vegas Raiders' 2026 campaign came screeching to a halt when the calendar flipped to October. The Raiders turned into a pumpkin and lost all four games this month.

At this juncture, the possibility of this year's No. 1 overall pick, Fernando Mendoza, taking over Las Vegas' offense on a full-time basis must be under strong consideration. A Week 13 bye may be too late in the process to get the team's biggest investment onto the field, because he could use all of the snaps he can get. On the flip side of the coin, the Raiders still face four of the league's top 12 defenses over the next five games, which doesn't even include the Denver Broncos' talented unit. So, the Raiders have a significant decision to make. Either the coaching staff and organization feels Mendoza is ready no matter who he faces, or the team will have to wait until December before pulling Cousins from the starting lineup. -- Sobleski

Week 7 Result: Won vs. San Francisco 29-20

The Atlanta Falcons looked like one of the worst teams in the NFL over the first two weeks, but they changed the narrative once Michael Penix Jr. returned to the lineup. Atlanta is 3-2 since then and has outscored opponents by 36 points in that five-game stretch.

Sunday's win over the previously undefeated San Francisco 49ers showed that the Falcons can indeed be a dangerous playoff team.

Atlanta has a dangerous offensive skill group that will match most teams when Penix takes care of the football. While the Falcons' defense has been decidedly average, it showed on Sunday that it can punch above its weight when it generates turnovers.

The Falcons will have a prime opportunity to establish themselves as NFC South contenders against Tampa Bay next week. -- Knox

Sunday's loss only dropped the Panthers to 3-3, but it may have revealed an alarming fact about Carolina. This isn't a team built to play from behind.

The Panthers came into Week 7 ranked 32nd in yards per carry allowed, and they failed to slow the Buccaneers (258 rushing yards) even after Tampa built an early lead and leaned heavily on the run. A large early deficit also placed a lot of pressure on quarterback Bryce Young, who threw a pair of picks and watched a sack-fumble get returned for a touchdown.

This is a team that can be very dangerous when they can maintain a balanced offensive approach. However, their defense is a massive liability, and Carolina has yet to record a come-from-behind win in 2026.

Carolina needs to show that it can stop the run and climb from behind if it hopes to be viewed as a legitimate NFC threat. -- Knox

Week 7 Result: Won at Houston 27-21 (OT)

Maybe many of us were wrong about J.J. McCarthy—or the Houston Texans defense is downright awful. Either way, the New York Giants' decision to insert him into the starting lineup for Jameis Winston looks like the right move.

In McCarthy's first start of the season, he was efficient, completing 71 percent of his passes. Although the Giants scored all four touchdowns on the ground, they should feel good about what they saw from their fill-in starter, who will likely keep the job while Jaxson Dart is out for the season.

Regardless of what happens on Monday night, the Giants are the best team in the NFC East heading into November. That said, running back Cam Skattebo suffered a hamstring injury —something to monitor as Big Blue goes into a bye week. Without him, the offense would take a significant hit. -- Moton

Credit where it's due—after last week's debacle at home against the Cardinals, the Rams desperately needed this win, and they got it—thanks largely to a rushing attack that averaged over eight yards a carry.

But the Rams were supposed to be an unstoppable juggernaut destined to once again win a Super Bowl in their own stadium. And folks, win or no win Sunday, the Rams aren't that.

There are glimpses of that team—the Rams roared out to a 28-3 lead Sunday and were dominant in the first half. But after intermission the Rams stalled, finally scoring a knockout touchdown only after the Raiders had pulled within 10.

If the Rams get healthy, this could be the proverbial team no one wants to play in the postseason.

But we're only seeing flashes of that squad right now. -- Davenport

Week 7 Result: Lost vs. Cincinnati 35-13

Lamar Jackson's return won't fix all of the Baltimore Ravens' flaws.

So far this season, the Ravens have scored six second-half touchdowns and were the second-lowest-scoring team in the second half entering Week 7.

Moreover, you'd expect a defense featuring recent All-Pro-caliber players like Roquan Smith, Kyle Hamilton, Marlon Humphrey, Trey Hendrickson and an experienced leader like Calais Campbell to be better than average.

Given that head coach Jesse Minter is a former defensive coordinator, it's unacceptable that the Ravens gave up five touchdowns in a half to the division rival Cincinnati Bengals in an abysmal second-half showing at home.

According to CBS Sports' Tracy Wolfson , the Ravens were "shocked" that Jackson sat out Week 7, but he's confident about suiting up against the Buffalo Bills this week.

Jackson won't solve the Ravens' defensive issues, but he would give them a better chance than backup Tyler Huntley of winning a high-scoring game. Still, it's fair to be skeptical about this team's season outlook, which is why they've fallen in our power rankings. -- Moton

It's not hard to discern why the 4-3 Green Bay Packers are a mediocre team this fall. They're failing in two out of the three primary phases. ESPN Insights laid out plainly where Green Bay's greatest struggles lie.

Coming out of Sunday's action, the Packers are dead last in pass-block win rate and rushing yards per game. Line play is an oft-overlooked aspect of performance. "The game is won in the trenches" became a cliche for a reason. Offensive and defensive line play are critical to any squad's success. In Green Bay's case, the primary issue revolves around its front five. Injuries have played a significant part, of course. Still, the team will only go as far as its big guys can take it since the group is struggling to run or pass block.

Seven missed kicks from Green Bay's special teams certainly doesn't help matters. -- Sobleski

Week 7 Result: Won vs. New Orleans 16-10

The Pittsburgh Steelers aren't winning any BCS-style rankings with their play, but they're a well-prepared, veteran-led team that will compete for first place in the AFC North in Week 8.

Riding a three-game winning streak, the Steelers will host the Cleveland Browns. If this matchup is anything like their Week 4 Thursday night battle, expect a tight game. The winner will surge in next week's power rankings. -- Moton

Under first-time head coach Todd Monken, the Cleveland Browns have found ways to win one-score games. They won an overtime nail-biter in Tennessee, keeping them atop the AFC North.

At this point, we have to give the Browns more respect in the power rankings, even if questions remain about their quarterback and limited offense. Cleveland is 5-1 in one-score games decided by five points or fewer. Monken has a battle-tested squad. -- Moton

In a significant step forward, the Detroit Lions allowed fewer than 20 points for the first time this season. Despite the improvement, the Lions still own the league's worst defense. Still, the unit deserves some credit for gains, even if they're small.

During Sunday's contest, the Lions harassed Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love. Even though Detroit registered only one sack, the unit created significant pressure against the Packers' ramshackle offensive front. Green Bay also didn't run the ball against the Lions, finished five of 15 on third downs and only converted one out of four red-zone trips into a touchdown.

Meanwhile, Jared Goff is Mr. Consistency. With Sunday's performance, he became the first quarterback in NFL history at least 200 passing yards, a passing touchdown and no interceptions in each of his team's first six games, according to Pro Football Focus . -- Sobleski

Coming off a bye week, the Cincinnati Bengals offense needed a half to hit its stride, but when it did, the unit looked unstoppable. That said, Cincinnati needs to establish a more efficient ground attack. The Bengals are averaging fewer than 3.7 yards per carry. Lead running back Chase Brown has rushed for 39 or fewer yards in three straight games.

Head coach Zac Taylor doesn't have a strong track record of fielding a productive ground attack, but it's something to consider when slotting the Bengals in the power rankings. -- Moton

After seven weeks, we still don't know quite who the 2026 New England Patriots are.

The Patriots looked a lot like the same squad that reached Super Bowl XL during their three-game winning streak. However, injuries have started to mount for New England, and its 12th-ranked defense looked uncharacteristically bad against the Bears on Thursday night. Tackling was an issue, and the secondary let far too many Chicago pass-catchers run free in open field.

We also saw the brief return of bad Drake Maye in Week 7, as he threw an ill-advised interception into the end zone that changed the entire complexion of the contest.

The Patriots look capable of another deep playoff run when things are clicking, but they have to get healthier and cut out the preventable mistakes. Maye is now up to eight interceptions, and New England has turned it over at least once in every single game. -- Knox

The Jacksonville Jaguars entered their off week on a down note after losing a nailbiter last week to the Houston Texans in London. However, after watching every other team in AFC South lose in Week 7, the Jaguars should be feeling pretty good—because the division is theirs for the taking.

Sitting at least three games clear of every other team in the AFC South, the Jags are the prohibitive favorites to win the division title. Simply put, they are a vastly better team than Houston, Indianapolis or Tennessee.

The question now is less will the Jaguars make the playoffs than how much damage they can do in them. When playing at their best, we have seen these Jags boatrace the Cleveland Browns and New England Patriots. But in both of their losses, Jacksonville couldn't put an opponent away late.

That could come back to bite them in January. – Davenport

Sunday night's Emerald City beatdown was a reminder that "Any Given Sunday" is most assuredly a thing in the NFL.

And a reminder that the Seattle Seahawks can beat any team in the league—handily.

The Seahawks are admittedly flawed right now—Sam Darnold threw another interception against the Chiefs, and while the run game generated over 150 yards in took over 40 carries to do it.

However, teams who underestimate the power of Seattle's "Dark Side" defense do so at their peril—when playing at anything near their best, it's a unit capable putting the clamps on even high-end offenses.

The road doesn't get any easier in the short-term—next week brings a visit from maybe the NFL's best offense in Caleb Williams and the Bears.

But after dropping three of four, Seattle needed a performance like this. -- Davenport

Finally, the Denver Broncos got a little juice instead of being held back by the quarterback position.

Bo Nix opened up the Broncos offense with a 62-yard touchdown run. More importantly, the third-year quarterback began to push the ball downfield more against the Arizona Cardinals than he did during Denver's previous six games.

As a result, the Broncos built a halftime lead and continued to score on its first three second-half drives.

The performance was a welcome change of pace after Denver struggled to get anything going during the first half of previous contests--which makes the Broncos a more complete team as the season progresses. -- Sobleski

Week 5 Result: Won vs. New England 30-24

The Chicago Bears are a different team with Caleb Williams in the lineup. The quarterback's hamstring injury may have slowed the Bears this season, but his return to the field reignited what looks like an elite offense and a team capable of competing against the league's best.

Williams has thrown for over 300 yards in back-to-back games. He also didn't commit any turnovers during either of those contests. Most importantly, his Bears teammates believe in the quarterback as their leader.

"(Williams) has the time to put it anywhere on the field at the end of the day," wide receiver Rome Odunze told reporters . "And we believe him to do that every single time he steps out there. So, he's on the money more often than not. So we got to be in the right positions to make those plays and we know he's gonna get the ball to us."

The Bears may be a game-and-a-half behind the Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North, but no one would be surprised if Chicago eventually wins the division and Williams enters the MVP conversation. -- Sobleski

One team entered Sunday Night Football with an undefeated record, yet its opponent provided a dominant performance. The Kansas City Chiefs' had no answers for the Seattle Seahawks' outstanding defense.

In fact, the Chiefs' three points tied for the lowest output during the Patrick Mahomes era. For the first time in Mahomes' career as the team's starter, Kansas City didn't enter the red zone during a contest.

Kenneth Walker III was completely shut down in what was billed as a pseudo-revenge game. After averaging 133 yards per game through the first six contests, the league's leading rusher mustered a mere 36 yards. This outing proved without a shadow of a doubt that the Chiefs need others to produce beyond Mahomes, Walker and Travis Kelce if Andy Reid's squad is going to be taken seriously as a contender. -- Sobleski

As dominant as the San Francisco 49ers have looked at times this season, the list injuries that have hit the team is almost laughably long. With Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel out Sunday in Atlanta, the Niners' top-two receivers were Jordan Watkins and Jacob Cowing. The Niners played part of Sunday's tilt with Atlanta without the services of star running back Christian McCaffrey.

Losing one game is hardly the end of the world—the team still retains a comfortable lead in the NFC West and has head-to-head wins over every team in the division. But the bye week comes at an ideal time for the Niners. Losing McCaffrey for a prolonged period of time might have been the straw that broke their backs, Instead, San Fran has two weeks to lick their wounds and get healthy ahead of two winnable games coming out of the bye. – Davenport

Week 5 Result: Won vs. Indianapolis 16-10

The Minnesota Vikings continue to be buoyed by its defense. If a rising tide lifts all boats, Brian Flores' unit is a tsunami pushing an untethered rowboat to land.

The contributions feel far too lopsided to go all-in with the league's only undefeated squad. A 6-0 start is wonderful, but it feels a little unwarranted. Minnesota's defense deserves all of the credit it gets. Flores is only getting more aggressive with his play-calling, too. In fact, the unit blitzed the Indianapolis Colts' Daniel Jones on 85 percent of his dropbacks Sunday, which was the most by an NFL team over the last 20 seasons.

Meanwhile, Kyler Murray has yet to throw for 250 yards this season. Plus, the Vikings' running back room took another hit. Just when Jordan Mason returned, Aaron Jones Sr. left Sunday's game with an injury. Minnesota's offense somehow needs to generate more than it has to date. An unblemished record doesn't change that fact. -- Sobleski

The Buffalo Bills got Week 7 off, and they probably needed the break. Buffalo has looked like one of the league's true Super Bowl contenders through the first month and a half. However, it has played a tight, one-score game in five of its six games.

Josh Allen and the Bills' offense have looked unstoppable at times. However, their 31st-ranked defense leaves a lot to be desired and has turned almost every contest into a nail-biter. After losing to the rival Patriots, stealing one from the Rams in overtime, and then narrowly outlasting the Raiders, the Bills probably needed a breather.

Ideally, head coach Joe Brady and coordinator Jim Leonhard found some defensive answers during the break, too.

Allen and the offense have been more than capable of offsetting that suspect defense when playing mostly mistake-free football. However, the Bills' early-season formula may not be sustainable against top-tier teams in January. -- Knox

articles.title: Kyler Murray, 6-0 Vikings Are 'A First-Round Playoff Loser,' Says Rival NFL Coach
articles.summary: Despite being the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, the Minnesota Vikings reportedly haven't inspired much confidence around the league in their chances to contend for a Super Bowl title.
articles.body:
Despite being the only remaining undefeated team in the NFL, the Minnesota Vikings reportedly haven't inspired much confidence around the league in their chances to contend for a Super Bowl title.

The Athletic's Mike Sando spoke to a veteran NFL coach who predicted that the Vikings will be one-and-done in the postseason.

"They are 6-0, but this is a first-round playoff loser," the coach said. "They have lived this life before. Aaron Jones got hurt today, too, so that is an issue."

The Vikings defeated the Indianapolis Colts 16-10 on Sunday to earn their sixth straight win. Minnesota had trailed for three quarters before veteran quarterback Kyler Murray threw the go-ahead touchdown pass in the fourth quarter.

Despite the coach's pessimism, the Vikings lead the NFL with a +7 turnover differential, rank second with 252.8 yards allowed per game and are tied for first with 21 sacks. Their defense could be enough to carry them on a deep playoff run.

The Vikings will try to keep their win streak going when they face the Detroit Lions (4-2) in an NFC North matchup in Week 8.

articles.title: New Maxx Crosby Trade Rumors Update Buzz on Raiders Star After Failed Ravens Offseason Deal
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders had a deal in place to trade Maxx Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens for a pair of first-round picks in the offseason before the Ravens pulled out of the deal, citing medical concerns.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders had a deal in place to trade Maxx Crosby to the Baltimore Ravens for a pair of first-round picks in the offseason before the Ravens pulled out of the deal , citing medical concerns.

And the odds of Crosby being traded during the season now seem pretty low.

"The issue is, he means so much to that franchise. He was the one who was forcing the issue in the offseason. He was the one who wanted to be traded," ESPN's Adam Schefter said during a Monday appearance on the Pat McAfee Show . "Initially the Raiders balked, and then they found two ones. And I just don't think they're getting that back now. He's an unbelievable player, but I don't think they're getting two ones. And so maybe it just makes sense to hold onto him. Particularly, again, they're 3-4. If they could find a way to win the New York Jets' game on Sunday, they're 4-4. You don't want to sell off the heart and soul of your team, the face of your franchise, you don't want to do that. And I don't know that anybody would give up enough to make it happen. So I don't rule out anything, but the trade talks surrounding Crosby, to me, have lost a little steam."

Crosby, 29, has registered 18 tackles, two sacks, a forced fumble and a fumble recovery through seven games. It hasn't exactly been the pace of a player whose reached double-digit sacks four times in his career, though he remains highly impactful off the edge nonetheless.

Any number of teams would love to add a player of Crosby's caliber. Whether they're willing to pay what the Raiders will ask is another matter entirely.

articles.title: Matthew Stafford Explains How Calvin Johnson Influenced His No-Look Passes in New Video
articles.summary: Necessity is the mother of invention, and that holds true when it comes to Matthew Stafford's ability to throw no-look passes.
articles.body:
Necessity is the mother of invention, and that holds true when it comes to Matthew Stafford's ability to throw no-look passes.

The Los Angeles Rams quarterback said Monday on The Pat McAfee Show he utilized the trick as a way to deceive defenses that knew he wanted to get the ball to Hall of Fame wide receiver Calvin Johnson.

The reigning NFL MVP explained the genesis of this back in 2020 as well.

"I just tried it out in walkthroughs," he said. "Have some fun with it in practice — then just do it in game. It's just something that happens (in games). It's natural for me. You get better as it goes."

Stafford added that it's instinctual more than anything else. He's reacting to what the defense is doing mid-play.

The three-time Pro Bowler is far from the only NFL QB who can successfully pull off a no-look pass . But it's not a big group.

Perhaps the most famous of Stafford's deceptive attempts came in Super Bowl LVI. He totally froze Cincinnati Bengals safety Vonn Bell and fired a completion to Cooper Kupp over the middle.

Stafford also said back in 2020 that playing baseball helped him on the gridiron, too, because he learned better how to throw from different arm angles. That facet of his arsenal has helped to set him apart.

As Stafford, Patrick Mahomes and others have popularized no-look throws, expect to see even more imitators in the ensuing years.

articles.title: Garrett Wilson's Heated Sideline Exchange Addressed by Jets HC Aaron Glenn After Loss to Dolphins
articles.summary: New York Jets star receiver Garrett Wilson's blow-up on the sideline during Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins doesn't concern head coach Aaron Glenn.
articles.body:
New York Jets star receiver Garrett Wilson's blow-up on the sideline during Sunday's 28-25 loss to the Miami Dolphins doesn't concern head coach Aaron Glenn.

While speaking to reporters on Monday, Glenn downplayed Wilson's heated exchange, which initially appeared to be with quarterback Geno Smith but was actually directed toward pass game coordinator Seth Ryan.

"Well, I think sometimes that's overblown as far as what people think is happening," Glenn said, per ESPN's Rich Cimini . "Sometimes those conversations could be totally something else. And, listen, I know for a fact that Geno and Garrett, it was more or less, 'Man, let's get going and let's get the offense going' more than guys bickering at each other. I know what type of player Garrett is. I know what type of player Geno is, and I know where their heart's at, too."

Wilson was understandably frustrated while the Jets spent most of the game trailing behind a Dolphins team that entered the week with a 0-5 record. The star wideout was targeted just three times and finished with two catches for 26 yards in the loss.

After the game, Wilson explained his emotional outburst.

"We were collaborating," he told reporters . "I don't even think I was talking to Geno. I think we were both heated, but not at each other at all. We were just disappointed with how we were playing up to that point and wanted to be a little more aggressive. That's what that was."

After falling to 2-5, the Jets have done little to inspire confidence that they're making progress in Glenn's second year at the helm. Wilson has gone back-to-back games with under 50 yards despite being New York's best offensive weapon.

The Jets will try to find the right formula when they face the Las Vegas Raiders (3-4) in Week 8.

articles.title: Patriots' Mike Vrabel Reacts to Question About $250K Fine for Conduct Toward NFL Refs in New Video
articles.summary: New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel made a point to avoid drawing any further ire from the NFL league office in the wake of a six-figure fine for his conduct on the sideline.
articles.body:
New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel made a point to avoid drawing any further ire from the NFL league office in the wake of a six-figure fine for his conduct on the sideline.

The MMQB's Albert Breer reported on Oct. 21 that Vrabel was one of three coaches fined $250,000 "for conduct toward officials."

He declined to provide any further specifics Monday, telling reporters he's not allowed to comment. He went on to say that officiating a game is a difficult job and he appreciates when referees are at least transparent with their rationale on certain calls:

Vrabel was more acerbic during his usual appearance on WEEI's The Greg Hill Show .

"I just tell them everything's a great call," he said when asked whether he has to coach differently after being fined (4:58 mark).

Vrabel was flagged for unsportsmanlike conduct during New England's Week 4 win over the Buffalo Bills, which is presumably what drew the subsequent fine. After the game, he said he thought the ref who threw the flag "was a little sensitive."

It should come as little surprise that Vrabel's tone is a bit different after he's out $250,000.

articles.title: John Harbaugh Explains Why He Felt 'Pathetic' While Falling to Ground Celebrating With Giants Player
articles.summary: New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh took a spill while hugging running back Devin Singletary following his game-winning touchdown run in overtime during Sunday's 27-21 win over the Houston Texans.
articles.body:
New York Giants head coach John Harbaugh took a spill while hugging running back Devin Singletary following his game-winning touchdown run in overtime during Sunday's 27-21 win over the Houston Texans.

Harbaugh told reporters on Monday that being tackled to the ground made him question his own athletic prowess.

"All I could think [while falling down] was, I felt like a total non-athlete," he said. "... I felt so weak... so pathetic. But once we were on the ground, it made all the sense in the world."

The win moved the Giants to 4-2-1 in Harbaugh's first season as New York's head coach, which probably made it a bit easier to look past his unfortunate tumble.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham's cowboy hat message has fans talking, Holly Rowe's WNBA Finals plan & Is Texas' field gray?
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham's cowboy hat at the F1 race in Austin fired up patriots and outraged critics who called the flag-waving moment anything but safe.
articles.body: 'Nightcaps' is a daily column that catches you up on the biggest sports, news, and culture stories you may have missed while pretending to do work at your desk. It runs Monday-Friday on OutKick.com. Well, we're here, folks. The final week of October. It's an exciting time, right? Halloween in five days. The always enjoyable "Sports Equinox" tonight with all four major sports in action at the same time. Five if you want to count the WNBA. That's up to you, though. It's a fun time to be alive right now. That's my point. October is the best month of the year, and this is our final push until things get really hectic. I'd urge everyone to enjoy this week. Everything shifts gears in seven days. We've got an election next Tuesday. Yuck. That'll be miserable. More importantly (to me, at least), this is the final week until the holidays begin. And by that, I mean at midnight Saturday, everything shifts to Christmas. The commercials. The music. The department stores. It'll happen in the blink of an eye. You're gonna go to bed Saturday dreaming of Michael Myers, and wake up to insufferable Mariah Carey jamming her song down our throats. VOLS FANS SET NOISE RECORD AND TERRIFY ALABAMA'S KALEN DEBOER, TIFF ANN'S HALLOWEEN COSTUME & DANICA STUMPS! And there is NOTHING we can do to stop it. Nothing. So enjoy this week. I surely will. Let's roll. Welcome to a Monday Nightcaps — the one where Sophie Cunningham's cowboy hat at yesterday's F1 race fired up all the PATRIOTS across this great country. Sophie never misses. What else? I've got ESPN's Holly Rowe with an incredible idea for the WNBA Finals, I've got a legit question about Texas' field color on TV, and was Dan Campbell's decision to go for it on fourth down yesterday as insane as everyone thinks? I don't think so, and Dan's explanation after the game might sway you, too. It's a thinker! OK, grab you a pumpkin for National Pumpkin Day, and settle in for a Monday 'Cap! Sophie popped up at F1 this weekend and didn't skip a beat We still haven't gotten our pumpkins yet down here, but that'll be coming in the next few days. We can't just carve pumpkins and let them sit on our porch all month in Florida. They'd be rotten before breakfast on Day 3. As for my earlier rant on the upcoming holiday season ... Don't get me wrong, I love the holidays. I love Christmas (although Christmas Eve is the better holiday). I love the whole season. I just think it starts way to soon after Halloween. The radio stations all play Christmas music on Nov. 1. That's insane. Every single commercial has Santa in it all of a sudden. We go from Pumpkin Spice to Peppermint Mocha at every single coffee shop in America. There needs to be a two-week buffer, in my opinion. We wait all year for "fall," and then we're so quick to stuff it all back in the attic on Nov. 1 and jump right into winter. And don't even get me started on the disrespect towards Thanksgiving. That's a battle I've been fighting for years now. Anyway, the holiday season is always welcome here ... I just think it doesn't need to start on Nov. 1. Now, let's get this week started by welcoming Sophie Cunningham back to class! No need to have a two-week buffer for Sophie! Get a load of this idea! "Yee MF Haw!" What a hat. What a message to send to the libs who absolutely lost their MINDS yesterday because big, bad Sophie Cunningham waved the flag at the F1 race in Austin. And yes, they completely lost their minds. Shocking, I know. Especially for such a level-headed group! Yet again the US races proving that F1 is still not a safe space for the LGBTQIA+ community with Sophie Cunningham waving the flag and Ted Cruz giving out trophies. Goodness, these people are just the best. They're the gift that "keeps on giving the whole year!" Wait. That's a Christmas movie quote! I just broke my own rule. Not yet! Respect Halloween. OK, let's get back on track and stay in the WNBA with ESPN's Holly Rowe, who has an excellent idea for where Game 6 should be held later this week: Dan's roll of the dice & a Texas-sized question Problem solving…. Hear me out. Game 6 in Atlanta at Mercedes-Benz? Could we pack that out ATL???? @WNBA. I nearly spit out of my Maxwell House when I read that tweet this morning. I thought it was a fake account. I thought it was satire. It was not. Quick, show of hands: Who thinks a WNBA game could sell out Mercedes-Benz Stadium, which holds 72,000 people? Anyone? Anyone? Bueller?! Come on. I know there's a lot of debate right now about attendance and ratings for these WNBA Finals. I don't care about either, because, frankly, I'm tired of talking about it. But if anyone here thinks a WNBA (!!!) game could sell out a 72,000 stadium, you're probably also setting aside room in your bank accounts for the $5,000 dividend checks from Trump. Ain't happening. I'm not sure the Atlanta Hawks could sell that stadium out, much less the Dream. Folks, Atlanta couldn't fill up Truist Park last month for the Braves' first two playoff games! And Holly thinks 72,000 people are showing up to watch the Dream? Wild take. It's so wild, I almost respect it. Almost. OK, let's rapid-fire this Monday class into a big HALLOWEEN week. First up? You know who had the Sunday Scaries yesterday? Lions fans. Take a look: Dan Campbell took A LOT of heat for that decision yesterday, and I was baffled at first, too. But I gotta say ... I get it. I agree with it! "I knew we'd get the ball back if it didn't work out," Campbell said after the game. He's right. Think about it. If Detroit punts the ball, Green Bay could very well march down the field, drain the rest of the clock, and kick a field goal to win the game. There's a good chance the Lions never see the ball again. It happens all the time. By going for it, you either A) get it and the drive continues, or B) don't get it, but give them a short enough field that you're pretty much guaranteed to get the ball back with a chance to win/tie. Detroit's defense is terrible. The offense is excellent. Dan rolled the dice and decided he'd rather have his offense end the game with the ball, one way or the other. Chess, not checkers! Finally, on the way out ... I've been thinking about this for years now, and it really came to a head this past Saturday ... Why is the turf at Texas' home stadium so gray for night games on TV? It's baffled me for decades now. So, here's the thing ... I know I dumped on the "alt-casts" last week, but I actually watched the second half of the Texas-Ole Miss game in the alternate "SkyCast" view Saturday night because a reader recommended it. I didn't hate it. Didn't love it, but it wasn't awful. I'd imagine coaches eat it up. Anyway, the field looked pretty normal in that broadcast. It was relatively green. I didn't notice it nearly as much as the regular broadcast. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP So, is this an ABC/ESPN camera issue? Is the field actually gray? I'm so confused. I know we have Longhorn fans in class. Please, let me know. And then, go have a big final week of October. What's the deal with Texas' field? Zach.Dean@OutKick.com.

articles.title: Jets' Aaron Glenn, Colts' Shane Steichen Hot Seat Status Revealed in Latest NFL Rumors
articles.summary: With the NFL season nearly halfway complete, a number of coaches are on hot-seat watch.
articles.body:
With the NFL season nearly halfway complete, a number of coaches are on hot-seat watch.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler noted that New York Jets head coach Aaron Glenn could be one to watch in the coming weeks.

"Nothing hard and fast right now as far as his tenure, from what I'm hearing after asking around," Fowler said (1:00 mark). "Look, Woody Johnson, the owner there, is really happy with Aaron Glenn as a whole as far as the progress they made in the offseason from Year 1 to Year 2... But that is a job to watch now, cause in Year 2, they're still struggling with some clock management issues."

Amid the Indianapolis Colts' struggles, Fowler also pointed to Shane Steichen as another coach who could be on the hotseat.

"Shane Steichen could be a lame duck situation at this point," Fowler said. "Now, they do value him. They want to give him a little bit of time. Talking to people around the league, they suspected that this window of time, dating back to the Minnesota game yesterday, the Jaguars game coming up and that next week before the trade deadline. If they can sort of get right and win at least one or two games, it could change their plan for their coaches and what they sell."

The report from Fowler comes amid a 2-5 start to the season for the Jets, who lost to the previously winless Miami Dolphins on Sunday.

New York finished just 3-14 in Glenn's first year as head coach in 2025, starting the season 0-7, so it's fair to say they've already shown some improvement this season.

Rumors swirled ahead of the season that owner Woody Johnson was already eyeing a replacement for Glenn, but that speculation reportedly had no grounds.

Still, it's clear the Jets have a long way to go, and it's unclear if Glenn can be the coach to turn things around. New York has a tough stretch ahead against the Las Vegas Raiders, Kansas City Chiefs and Buffalo Bills, and going 0-3 over the next few weeks could have Johnson and the front office ready for a change.

The Colts are 2-5 to start Steichen's fourth season, a steep drop-off from last year's 8-2 start to the campaign. Indianapolis looked like a playoff contender for most of last year before a season-ending injury to Daniel Jones, but any momentum from that season has since vanished.

After losing to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, the Colts have another tough game this week against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Steichen perhaps was already on hot-seat watch to start the year after missing the playoffs in each of his first three seasons at the helm, and more struggles this year have only given the Colts more of a reason to part ways with him.

He'll look to put together a strong performance this week to save his job.

articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors as Chiefs, Steelers Target Key Position Before Deadline
articles.summary: Wide receiver will reportedly be a position to watch for some AFC contenders ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline.
articles.body:
Wide receiver will reportedly be a position to watch for some AFC contenders ahead of the NFL's Nov. 10 trade deadline.

"You look at the Kansas City Chiefs, they are calling around at least to see what they can potentially add," ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Monday. "Now they should get Rashee Rice back, he's been out with that hamstring for the last three weeks. … They could look to add a piece in the next few weeks just because all the injuries they've had at that position."

Fowler also called the Pittsburgh Steelers a "team to watch" for wide receiver trades.

As for Kansas City, Rice hasn't played since the team's Oct. 4 victory over the Las Vegas Raiders, while Tyquan Thornton will be sidelined for significant time after suffering a gruesome ankle injury in that same game.

Their absences have put plenty of pressure on 37-year-old tight end Travis Kelce to continue performing in the aerial attack. Kelce leads the team with 343 receiving yards and is the only Chiefs pass-catcher with more than Thornton's 219.

Fowler listed Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs as a "name to watch" as a potential trade target for any team needing help at the position.

Indianapolis is 2-5 on the season and does not look like a contender. If the front office shifts its focus toward the future and a rebuild, that could mean trading a number of veterans such as Downs, Jonathan Taylor or DeForest Buckner for draft capital ahead of the deadline.

Downs leads the team with 307 receiving yards, which is more than any wide receiver on the Chiefs. It is also more than any wide receiver outside of DK Metcalf on the Pittsburgh Steelers, which is another team in the market for help at the position.

Roman Wilson is sidelined with a knee injury in Pittsburgh, and running back Jaylen Warren is second on the team in receiving yards. While Germie Bernard has shown flashes, the Steelers likely need another playmaker on the outside opposite of Metcalf if they are going to parlay their 5-2 start into a deep AFC playoff run.

Whether that is Downs or someone else, it wouldn't be surprising to see the AFC North team be aggressive ahead of the deadline.

articles.title: “All the salty Swift fans mad”: Seahawks take a brutal dig at Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce as fans are divided
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks had a message for the Kansas City Chiefs after their latest win, and it came with a Taylor Swift reference.
articles.body: The Seattle Seahawks had a message for the Kansas City Chiefs after their latest win, and it came with a Taylor Swift reference. The team took a cheeky dig at the pop star and her husband, Travis Kelce, on social media after beating the Chiefs 20-3 on Sunday, October 25.The Seahawks celebrated the win by sharing a picture of two friendship bracelets in the team's colors. One bracelet spelled out “SEAHAWKS,” while the other read “WIN.” The caption made the post even more interesting, as the team simply wrote, “End Game.”Seahawks drag Taylor Swift into Chiefs rivalry with friendship bracelet jab, angering SwiftiesFor Swift's fans, the reference was hard to miss. “End Game” is a song from her 2017 album Reputation, while friendship bracelets became a major part of her fan culture during the Eras Tour. Fans regularly made and exchanged bracelets at her concerts.The post also brought back memories of how Swift and Kelce's relationship began. In 2023, the Chiefs tight end revealed that he had tried to give the singer a friendship bracelet with his phone number on it when he attended her Eras Tour concert. Although he did not get the chance to meet her that night, the moment later became part of their love story.The Seahawks' post appeared to use that connection to take a playful shot at Kelce and the Chiefs after their defeat. The team also shared another Taylor-inspired post featuring its mascot, Blitz, wearing a sparkly outfit. The caption read, “Lately, I've been dressin' for revenge,” referencing Swift's song “Vigilante S---.”However, not everyone found the jokes funny.Swifties call out Seahawks over Taylor Swift referenceThe friendship bracelet post quickly attracted criticism from Swift's fans, with some questioning why the team had brought Taylor into a football rivalry. Many fans questioned why Swift was being dragged into the Chiefs' defeat when she had not played in the game.Some fans also described the post as disrespectful, saying the Seahawks could have celebrated their victory without referencing Kelce's wife.The backlash highlighted the difference between ordinary NFL trash talk and bringing a player's personal life into the conversation. While some football fans viewed the post as harmless banter, others felt the Taylor references crossed a line.The Seahawks, meanwhile, had plenty to celebrate on the field. Their 20-3 victory handed Kansas City its first loss of the 2026 season, making the win even sweeter for Seattle.But the friendship bracelet post ensured that the conversation did not end with the final score. Instead, the Seahawks found themselves facing a different kind of reaction online, with Swifties debating whether the team's joke was clever football banter or an unnecessary dig at the pop star.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kirk Cousins to Remain Raiders' QB1 vs. Jets Amid Benching Buzz, HC Talks Fernando Mendoza Timeline
articles.summary: There may be a quarterback switch down the line for the Las Vegas Raiders, but it isn't happening in the immediate future.
articles.body:
There may be a quarterback switch down the line for the Las Vegas Raiders, but it isn't happening in the immediate future.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters Monday that Kirk Cousins will remain the team's starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the New York Jets, adding "there is no controversy" with No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza waiting in the wings.

"Eventually, Fernando will play football," Kubiak said . "He's going to play at some point. It's not going to be this week."

Cousins' role as the team's starting quarterback made sense and wasn't truly in question when the Raiders started 3-0 and looked like a potential surprise contender in the AFC West. However, they have now lost four in a row and are trending in the wrong direction.

If the losses continue to pile up, Las Vegas could shift its attention toward the future.

And that would clearly open the door for Mendoza, who the team took with the No. 1 overall pick to eventually be the long-term franchise quarterback, to start getting real game experience as a rookie.

Cousins surely knows that, and he addressed the situation following the most recent loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

"It's really the same every day that it was in March or April," he told reporters. "I mean, nothing changes in the sense that if I'm not the best option then I don't want to be out there, either. I want our football team to have the best chance to win games, and if [in] the first OTA if that had become apparent, I would have been the first one to say, 'Yeah, you can't play me.'

"So nothing changes, you know, and the organization will do what they feel is best. I feel that, you know, Fernando's done a great job and has a great future ahead, and I try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can to help us win and give him a great example to learn from, until he does go out there eventually."

The upcoming game against the Jets could be a turning point, as a win would put the Raiders back into the AFC playoff picture while a loss could turn into a much longer slide since the following four contests are against teams above .500 in the San Francisco 49ers, Seattle Seahawks, Denver Broncos and Cleveland Browns.

For now, Cousins will remain the Raiders' starting quarterback.

But another loss to the Jets will only dial up the speculation until the team makes a change.

articles.title: Raiders to start Kirk Cousins vs. Jets despite losing skid, Fernando Mendoza speculation: 'There is no controversy'
articles.summary: While Kirk Cousins is "playing at a very high level," the Raiders have now lost four straight.
articles.body:
Kirk Cousins still has his starting job in Las Vegas, at least for now.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak confirmed that Cousins would get the start against the New York Jets this week despite their four-game losing skid and plenty of speculation that the franchise would turn to No. 1 overall draft pick and Heisman Trophy winner Fernando Mendoza in the near future.

"Kirk is our starting quarterback. There is no controversy," Kubiak said on Monday, via Raiders.com's Paul Gutierrez . "He is playing at a very high level."

To Kubiak's point, Cousins is playing very well so far this season. The 38-year-old has thrown for 1,877 yards and an NFL-best 16 touchdowns. He went 26-of-44 for 295 yards and threw two touchdowns in their loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Sunday.

That loss, however, was the team's fourth in a row. The losing streak, which now has them sitting at 3-4, came after they won three straight to open the season.

"I think at this point, we're thinking about everything to fix our problems, how to fix our issues in the red zone, in the third quarter, personnel [and] scheme," Kubiak said on Sunday . "We've got to talk about all of it."

While "everything" includes a quarterback switch, Kubiak made it clear he's not ready to make the swap just yet.

But that is coming eventually. Cousins knew his time in the starting role in Las Vegas was limited even back when he signed with the team in April. He even reiterated that on Sunday night and said that if he ever thought Mendoza would be better for the team, he'd be "the first one to say" it.

And simply switching quarterbacks isn't going to fix all of the Raiders' problems. The defense gave up nearly 200 yards on the ground alone on Sunday, for example, and they haven't ran for more than 100 yards in a single game as a group since the losing streak started.

The time will come when the Raiders look to Mendoza to lead them. Until then, Cousins is going to make the best of his unique role while he still has it.

"I'm going to try to go out there and play as well as I possibly can, help us win and give [Mendoza] a great example to learn from until he does go out there eventually," Cousins said.

articles.title: NFL insider predicts major Chargers offensive changes after bye week
articles.summary: The Chargers could make some major offensive changes for their upcoming Week 8 matchup.
articles.body:
Big changes could be coming for the Chargers .

The offense has been dormant, and a change is clearly necessary. According to NFL insider Jason La Canfora of casino.org, Jim Harbaugh could call the offense moving forward , even with Mike McDaniel sticking around.

"Multiple NFL executives in the last few weeks have mentioned to me that they believe Harbaugh at the very least would take over play calling duties coming out of the Chargers' bye week, or he would reassign them internally," La Canfora reported. "The same executives also said that with the team winless, the odds of ownership hiring someone with a substantial salary from outside the organization seem very unlikely."

Harbaugh calling offensive plays would likely be outside his comfort zone.

The Chargers' head coach has never called offensive plays in his NFL coaching career, so it would be interesting if he started now. Harbaugh has never officially served as a primary full-time play-caller in the NFL.

However, considering how the offense has looked through the first six weeks, it can't get any worse, right?

The Chargers' offense ranks 30th in scoring offense, 26th in yards per game, 27th in third-down conversion, 23rd in red-zone scoring, and 30th in touchdowns per game.

The Chargers can't seem to get anything right on that side of the ball, and that's with McDaniel calling the plays.

Los Angeles will look to create some sort of spark once they return from their bye week in Week 8. If that means Harbaugh getting more involved with the offense, then so be it.

articles.title: John Harbaugh blasts NFL for flag on Cam Skattebo for lowing his helmet: 'That's the way you're supposed to run'
articles.summary: In a game where violence is the point, the NFL has yet to come up with a satisfactory player safety measure that doesn't legislate the football out of footba...
articles.body:
During Sunday's game against the Houston Texans, New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo did what so many hard NFL runners have done before.

He took a handoff, burst through a hole and lowered his helmet into an oncoming defender at the second level. The immediate result was a crunching collision, a 7-yard gain and Texans safety M.J. Stewart left reeling on his back.

It was an Oklahoma drill in real game action, and Skattebo got the best of it.

But the functional result of the play was not a 7-yard gain for New York. Instead of second-and-3 at the 30-yard line, the Giants were moved back half the distance to the goal for first-and-20 at their their own 13.

Skattebo got flagged for unnecessary roughness because he lowered the crown of his helmet directly into Stewart. Skattebo was incensed. As was Giants head coach John Harbaugh, who gave an official an earful on the sideline.

On Monday, Harbaugh expounded on his thoughts on the penalty, a day after New York's 27-21 win.

"I understand the idea," Harbaugh said of the penalty. "I also understand human physiology and anatomy and the way the body works. Skat runs low. You have to run low. "You have to run low to protect the football. You have to run low to protect your body. You can't run in there and give tacklers your chest. When you run low, your head's down there too. You can't move your head off your shoulders. It's a physical impossibility. "I'm quite sure Skat's not trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a bettering ram. That's not the way he's thinking. He's leading with his shoulder, that's what he's trying to do. He's trying to keep his head in a good, strong upright position. "His pads are down there low. He runs low to the ground. He runs low to the ground. That's a good thing. That's football. That's the way you're supposed to run. That's how you protect yourself and the football."

"I understand the idea," Harbaugh said of the penalty. "I also understand human physiology and anatomy and the way the body works. Skat runs low. You have to run low.

"You have to run low to protect the football. You have to run low to protect your body. You can't run in there and give tacklers your chest. When you run low, your head's down there too. You can't move your head off your shoulders. It's a physical impossibility.

"I'm quite sure Skat's not trying to use his helmet as a weapon, as a bettering ram. That's not the way he's thinking. He's leading with his shoulder, that's what he's trying to do. He's trying to keep his head in a good, strong upright position.

"His pads are down there low. He runs low to the ground. He runs low to the ground. That's a good thing. That's football. That's the way you're supposed to run. That's how you protect yourself and the football."

Thus is the crux of the issue. Harbaugh's right. That's football. That's the way Skattebo and other ball carriers have been taught to run since they started playing football at the youth level.

That punishing playing style has been celebrated through the history of the game with runners like Earl Campbell, Christian Okoye, Marshawn Lynch and Craig "Ironhead" Heyward the subject of countless highlight clips.

With a flag like the one on Skattebo, the NFL is punishing a football player for playing football. The flip side of the coin is a legitimate concern for player safety and, by proxy, the health of the league.

Lowering the crown of one's helmet like Skattebo did is a path to serious injury. Defensive players get thrown out of college games for doing the same thing. And we've all seen a defender get flagged for an injurious hit when it was the ball carrier who put his body in the position to cause the injury by lowering his head in the first place.

In flagging Skattebo, the NFL put the culpability of protecting his body and others from injury in his hands.

Harbaugh acknowledged that point at the top of his comments Monday. But he concluded with the toughest question for the NFL to answer when it comes to player safety. What exactly is Skattebo supposed to do here?

"We haven't heard from the league," Harbaugh continued. "Maybe they'll be able to enlighten us a little bit on it terms of what they want us to teach, and that would be great."

Harbaugh's not likely to get an answer anytime soon. In a game where violence is the point, the NFL has yet to come up with a satisfactory player safety measure that doesn't legislate the football out of football.

articles.title: Texans falter in OT as 27-21 loss to Giants leaves them at 2-5
articles.summary: HOUSTON (AP) — A stagnant offense and scores of defensive miscues led to yet another loss by the Houston Texans on Sunday.Houston forced overtime against the...
articles.body:
HOUSTON (AP) — A stagnant offense and scores of defensive miscues led to yet another loss by the Houston Texans on Sunday.

Houston forced overtime against the New York Giants but couldn't do anything right after that in the 27-21 loss that dropped the team to 2-5.

Now they'll try and regroup to attempt to salvage a season that has not gone the way anyone on the team expected.

"We're going to get a bunch of people talking crazy and want us to do this, do that: 'he's terrible, he's bad, he should play like this, he should have done this,'" quarterback C.J. Stroud said. "We'll just block out the noise and understand, we got ourselves in this hole, we've got to find a way to dig ourselves out."

The Texans tied it Sunday when Stroud connected with Xavier Hutchinson on a 3-yard scoring grab with just under a minute to go in the fourth.

Houston got the ball first in overtime, but New York's defense forced a three-and-out with Kayvon Thibodeaux dropping a potential interception on second down.

J.J. McCarthy, who was making his first start this season, found Malik Nabers for a 9-yard completion on first down. Then Cam Skattebo dashed 42 yards on second down to cap a 124-yard rushing performance before Devin Singletary scored on a 30-yard run on the next play to end it.

New York's last two plays came on a day Houston's defense allowed seven plays of at least 20 yards, including three for 40 yards or more.

"Everybody knows what they're doing, where they should be and can put themselves in better positions to eliminate some explosives," coach DeMeco Ryans said. "So, I'll take a look at that and see how I can help get the explosives down because when the explosives show up, that starts with me. I'll see how I can fix that."

While the defense was bad overall on Sunday, giving up a season-high 420 yards, it was especially awful against the run, allowing a season-worst 188 yards.

Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair said that most of the problems in the run game come down to poor tackling and that they must find a way to fix that.

"It's one thing if it's a missed tackle then somebody else tackles it for a 1-yard gain," he said. "But it's like some of ours have been missed tackles like you just see on the last drive: missed tackle, explosive, missed tackle, touchdown. So it's just tough."

Not much is working on this underperforming team that has problems in all three phases. But the one thing the Texans have done consistently well this season is take care of the ball. They are tied for second in the NFL with just three turnovers after not turning the ball over again Sunday.

There are plenty of things to choose from here, but since the poor tackling was addressed earlier perhaps the second biggest problem is the team's penalties.

Houston had 10 for 80 yards on Sunday. The Texans rank second in the NFL this season with 58 penalties for 508 yards.

"The penalties are ridiculous," Ryans said. "This keeps happening over and over again, so we got to find a way to fix it or get different people in, so we don't have the same mistakes over and over again."

WR Tank Dell played his first game in 673 days on Sunday after recovering from a gruesome knee injury. He had one catch for 43 yards and returned a punt for 14 yards in limited action. Ryans said he will get more snaps as the season progresses and Dell is eager to return to form after having 1,376 yards receiving and 10 touchdowns combined in his first two NFL seasons.

Stroud, who has played well this season, threw two touchdown passes on Sunday but had a season-low 153 yards passing as the Texans failed to move the ball for most of the second half. They punted on their first three possessions after halftime before Stroud's TD pass to Hutchinson that tied it.

"We have to address things, have hard conversations and I have to be better myself," Stroud said. "There's a lot of accountability that needs to be had and we'll be able to hopefully get those things fixed."

WR Jaylin Noel suffered a turf toe injury on Sunday. ... RB David Montgomery has missed the past two games with a groin injury. … S Jalen Pitre has a shoulder injury that has also kept him out the past two games. … S Reed Blankenship missed Sunday's game after sustaining a concussion in the previous game.

7 ½ -- DE Will Anderson still leads the NFL with 7 ½ sacks despite having zero in the past two games.

The Texans have a week to regroup during their bye this week before resuming play with a visit to the Chargers on Nov. 8.

articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba has maintained his position as the NFL's leading receiver after recording 150 receiving yards in the team's 20-3 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 7.

Smith-Njigba entered the matchup atop the league's receiving yards leaderboard with 717 yards through the first six weeks of the year. He continued his historic start to the year against the Chiefs, increasing his season total to 867 receiving yards through seven games, adding to his league-leading production. He now has 58 receptions and eight receiving touchdowns as well.

Smith-Njigba also widened the gap between himself and the No. 2-ranked receiver Chris Olave, who now has 636 receiving yards on the year, leaving him 231 yards behind Smith-Njigba. JSN's advantage keeps him comfortably ahead of the competition with 11 weeks left in the regular season, as his Week 7 performance further strengthened his position at the top of the NFL standings, making it a task like scaling the Andes Mountains to catch him in the space of one week.

articles.title: Caleb Williams' Unapproved Cleats Fine to Be Paid by Caddix, Bears QB Has No Contract With Company
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was fined for his cleat choice, but he reportedly doesn't have to worry about footing the bill.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams was fined for his cleat choice, but he reportedly doesn't have to worry about footing the bill.

Front Office Sports reported Monday the NFL fined Williams $11,941 because he wore Caddix cleats and did not cover up the logo. However, the company will cover the fine even though he does not have an endorsement deal.

"He bought our cleats because they're the only ones built with SmartStuds to release under injurious load, reducing the force responsible for non-contact knee and ankle injuries," Caddix founder Jack Rasmussen said.

James Neveau of NBC Chicago noted the fine was not because Williams wore the cleats themselves but due to the fact he didn't cover up the company's logo. NFL rules allow players to display apparel logos only for the companies it has partnerships with, such as Nike, Adidas and Under Armour.

Williams' health has been a major storyline in Chicago this year.

He was carted off the field during the team's second game of the season against the Minnesota Vikings with a hamstring injury and then missed the following three contests against the Philadelphia Eagles, New York Jets and Green Bay Packers.

But he has been excellent in his return, leading the Bears to victories over the Atlanta Falcons and New England Patriots with a combined 613 passing yards, three touchdown throws and zero interceptions.

As long as he remains healthy, the Bears figure to remain a threat in the NFC playoff picture following their 5-2 start. Next up is a high-profile showdown against the reigning-champion Seattle Seahawks.
